note: Unbaked. Extracted from data/scenes-ch19.js (memory pages first, then scenes in order). New speakers needing cast entries: Oblivion Censor, Dead-Letter Office (narration), Mrs. Alvarez, Floor 59 (narration). Battle lines are in data/ch19-battle.js.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: This is my first meet. I was seven. I looked at the bleachers and there was one empty folding chair at the very front, on the aisle, and then there was Tata in it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He was an hour early. He had a thermos. He said the aisle seat is for the person who cheers the loudest. Then he did not cheer at all. He said “Mm.” It was the loudest Mm of my whole life.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I fell off the beam. It is four inches wide. It does not care about me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The beam is four inches. You are nine. Both of those are fine.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He said it like it was a fact on a form. I got back up because it sounded official.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Before every routine I gave him my Sparkling Diamond Gold Soup Dumpling squishy to hold. Nobody else is allowed to hold it. It is very important and slightly sticky.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He has put it in his coat pocket at every single meet since. It has been through three coats. He says it has “seniority.” I am going to put it somewhere he will trip on it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Shoulder rides. The ceiling is so close up here. You can touch it if you stretch.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Duck.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I ducked. He did not duck. We hit the lamp. It was the best day of my life, and I was in a hospital hallway.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Bedtime. Tata reads to Lamby, not to me. Lamby likes dragons. Tata does the dragon voice like a man filing his taxes.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I laughed so hard I got the hiccups. He said “That is not on the schedule.” He wrote HICCUPS on his hand with a pen.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: At the airport I tied a pink ribbon around his wrist. I said, come back with the same wrist.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He did. He kept the ribbon in his wallet next to his library card. He said he checks it out regularly.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Backyard races. I won every one until I was twelve. Then I found out why.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I made him run it again, for real. He lost again. Honestly. My big brother, the slowest man on Long Island, and he looked so proud.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mile twenty of my first marathon. I was falling apart. And there was Tom on the curb with a thermos and a sign.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The sign said: AMY. GO. (I HAVE NO SIGN WORDS.) I cried. I ran the last six miles in a rage. Best six miles of my life.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Every long run, he asked my time. I thought he was being polite.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: There is a notebook in his desk. Every time, every run, in his awful handwriting, with a little star next to the fast ones. He never told me. He just kept the numbers.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Our first date. He had a mug with a broken handle and he was drinking out of it anyway, holding the pieces.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I fixed it right there with gold. A seam you can see. He said, “Does it work?” I said, “It works better now.” He looked at me like I had said something in a language he had been waiting for.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He used to sit in the studio and read while I threw pots. Hours. Not a word.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Once he looked up and said I looked like a man doing nothing very carefully. I said, “You really wheel know me.” He groaned so beautifully. I am keeping that groan forever.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My first cup. Lopsided. The handle is much too big. I made it for him and then I was embarrassed and hid it in a drawer.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He found it. He has used it every morning since. Every morning, same cup. He says it holds exactly the right amount of coffee. It does not. It holds too much. That is the point.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Here. You are not allowed to forget this. I put it right where you will trip on it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Come back with the same wrist, Tata. I tied it already. You just have to come.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Time starts when you get here, Tom. I will be the one standing at the line, yelling.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hey. You left your coffee. It is still warm, I think. Come get it.

lines.speaker: Dead-Letter Office
lines.text: Far off, in the hub, a brass bell rings by itself. Four lights are on at the Claim Desk. It is time.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It has been eleven hours. I have made coffee four times. I have not drunk any of it. That is not like me.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Plan. Mom and Dad are stone. Tom is somewhere the Loom does not have a place for. And there is one place in this city that keeps everything nobody could put anywhere.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The post office. We already said that.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Nara found it first.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara is sitting very straight in front of Tom’s mailbox, and she is staring into the slot. She has not blinked. A thin gold light is coming out of the slot, like a sleeping lamp.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That is not a regular mailbox. That is a mailbox that is thinking about something.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s his. It’s the mailbox at the bottom of his steps, where his bills and my birthday cards go. It’s warm.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: If you drop a letter in a mailbox and it goes nowhere... where does it go?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Down. I think it goes down.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Whoa. It’s a post office for things that don’t have anywhere to go.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Dead letters. Every undelivered thing in the city ends up under it. Birthday cards. Thank-you notes. One pretzel.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That’s MY pretzel. I mean Rose’s. Rose’s pretzel. For Deedee.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Look at the big ledger. There’s a page for Second Avenue. There’s a blank rectangle where a name should be.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s still wet. Somebody erased him and left the space, like they were going to write somebody else in.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Four doors. One for each of us.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: People who would not forget him. That’s the whole job description.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The desk in the middle has four little brass niches in the front. Four of us, four niches. And a chair that someone just stood up out of.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There’s a thermos on it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s his. I would know that thermos in the dark.

lines.speaker: Dead-Letter Office
lines.text: Four keepsakes glow in four brass niches. The bell sits on the counter. Rose reaches up, stands on her tiptoes, and rings it.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: Good evening. The Office is closed. May I help you? You look lost, which is the right way to look in here.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We’re here for a name. A man named Tom, on Second Avenue.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I have one clean line on a page. I have a name that is too loud for it. I was tidying. It is not personal. I tidy everything that does not fit.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He is my brother.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I am sure he is lovely. He is also unclaimed. Everything here is. That is the best a thing can be, Mrs. Gregori: safe and unclaimed.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can’t erase somebody because he doesn’t fit your form.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: It is the only thing I am for. No one has ever handed me a letter to deliver. They only hand me returns.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: That’s the saddest job in the world.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: It is a very tidy job.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: Please step back from the desk. I will write the name out.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. We can do this again. It’s a pottery rule: the first one always cracks.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: The Censor lowers his stamp. The black bar over his face slides to the side, a little at a time, and under it is only a small tired man with ink on his cuffs.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I have never been argued with by so many people at once. It was... full.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sorry I was late. I was written out of the schedule. I’ll sort it out with accounting.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: TATA!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: TATA!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello. Hello. Yes. Careful of the glasses. The glasses have been through a lot.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You absolute marshmallow. You were GONE. You ate nothing. You skipped lunch for a whole afternoon, and then a night.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I had a granola bar. It was written out too. I haven’t felt this hungry since the nineties.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara arrives at about a hundred miles an hour and climbs directly onto Tom. Nobody tries to stop her.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. I know. I missed you too. I was a small gold light and I missed you the whole time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He turns to the Censor, who is looking at the floor.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You have never delivered anything.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Rose.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Here. It’s a little bit squished. It’s for Deedee. It was held for pickup, but nobody picked it up, because she’s stone.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It is a first-timer’s route. One pretzel. One tower. Fifty-nine floors up, and then a grandmother.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I do not... I have never left the Office.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The route is not far. The job is only to put a thing in someone’s hands. You are already very good at the part where you carry it.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: The Censor takes the pretzel in both hands, carefully, as if it were made of glass. Then he lifts his stamp, looks at it, and brings it down on the napkin. It does not say RETURN TO SENDER. It says DELIVERED.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: It is a nicer word to hold than I expected.

lines.speaker: Dead-Letter Office
lines.text: In the big ledger, the clean white rectangle fills itself in, one slow letter at a time. T. O. M. The ink is the exact blue of a thermos cap.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. Home. Food. Then Mom and Dad. In that order.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: In that order.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stone does not respond to talking. I have checked. Stone responds to being warm for a long time with people nearby.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom’s rule: a house is warm when somebody is cooking in it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So we cook.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A lot. We cook a LOT.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Tom! You’re BACK. I saw the light on at four a.m. and I thought, he’s home, and then I thought, no, that’s a different kind of light. I made a lasagna.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: I brought a rock. Lachlan picked it out. Isla ate a different rock. We are keeping a close eye on it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you. All of you. I will put the rock on the mantel.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: I heard there was a situation. I brought lemon bars. And peppers. My nephew grows them. They are very hot. A man called Boppy would know what to do.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy would eat one raw and say it was “fine” in a voice.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The kitchen is a mess. Every pot is in use. The window is fogged. It smells like a Sunday.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The oven door handle came off. I fixed it. You could say I handled it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Please stop.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lasagna, eleven minutes. Lemon bars, six. I have a timer on everything. Nobody is allowed to be late for this.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I choreographed the pasta. It goes from the pot to the plate in a very specific arc.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I am the taster. I have tasted nine times. It’s for quality.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The pasta does not go in an arc.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It goes in an arc if you believe in it, Tata.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He looks at the table. Everyone he loves is crowded around it, and somebody has put a rock in the middle like a centerpiece. He doesn’t say anything for a second.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Pack it up. Sal is waiting outside with cab seven. We are going to the Glass Tower, and we are bringing dinner.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in. Bring the lasagna on your lap, it holds the heat. Fifty-nine floors, no stops, I am not even charging. I am scared of that tower and I am going anyway.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The snow globe is still on its plinth. Inside it, very small, two stone figures hold each other up. The amber light is crawling on their hands. It is slower than before.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom. Dad. We brought dinner.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I brought a pretzel. It has been DELIVERED. It has a stamp.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Everybody sit. Around the plinth. Nobody leave. Plates on laps.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Steam from the lasagna drifts across the glass. The amber light turns the color of toast. A crack of warm yellow runs along the stone, then two, then nine.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s working. It’s working!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Oh. Oh, my back. My back is going to be talking about this for a week.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is that lasagna? Who made lasagna? Who has been in my kitchen?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: DEEDEE! BOPPY!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh, my babies. Come here. All of you. Come here, to the moon and back and back and back.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Which one of you is eating the peppers raw?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Nobody. Yet.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Hand me one. For my knees.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everyone is crowded onto one floor of a glass tower with plates in their laps, and for a minute, it is just a family having dinner, eight people and a dog.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom. Who is the man in the gold coat? The one who kept us on a shelf?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Vance. He is still up there, at the top. He is going to want more than a shelf.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then we finish eating first.

lines.speaker: Floor 59
lines.text: Overhead, through the glass ceiling, every clock in the sky stops. They are all pointing at the same minute: the one just after the last. A door nobody has noticed before, high up in the tower, has begun to open.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He sets down his plate. Then he picks it back up.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Seconds first. Then the sky.
